lines.trans: Good morning to all early viewers of our show!
With you again is your favorite show Delicious Morning.
Today we will prepare simple appetizing sunny-side-up eggs.

words.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

lines.trans: Every morning opens a new day before us.
We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.
Sometimes simple things turn out to be the most important.
We add a little butter and salt.
We often look for complex answers to questions.
A few minutes and a wonderful breakfast is ready!
The main thing is never to miss your opportunities.
Fate might not give us a second chance.
Bon appetit and have a good day everyone!
Value every moment of your real life.
Good morning to all early viewers of our show!
With you again is your favorite show Delicious Morning.
Today we will prepare simple appetizing sunny-side-up eggs.

lines.trans: Every morning opens a new day before us.
We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.
Sometimes simple things turn out to be the most important.
We add a little butter and salt.
We often look for complex answers to questions.
A few minutes and a wonderful breakfast is ready!
The main thing is never to miss your opportunities.
Fate might not give us a second chance.
Bon appetit and have a good day everyone!
Value every moment of your real life.
Good morning to all early viewers of our show!
With you again is your favorite show Delicious Morning.
Today we will prepare simple appetizing sunny-side-up eggs.

words.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

lines.trans: Every morning opens a new day before us.
We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.
Sometimes simple things turn out to be the most important.
We add a little butter and salt.
We often look for complex answers to questions.
A few minutes and a wonderful breakfast is ready!
The main thing is never to miss your opportunities.
Fate might not give us a second chance.
Bon appetit and have a good day everyone!
Value every moment of your real life.
Value every moment of your real life.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'appetite', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!
He has a good appetite.
Your porridge. Enjoy your meal.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('appetizing, delicious').

examples.trans: This is a very appetizing breakfast.

examples.text: Сегодня мы приготовим простую аппетитную глазунью.
examples.trans: Today we will prepare simple appetizing sunny-side-up eggs.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to take', forming an aspectual pair with 'взять'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.
He doesn't take bribes.
I'm not taking the knife.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.trans: It's an important question.
I have important business.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('magnificent, splendid').

examples.trans: This is magnificent, splendid.
A magnificent idea from an unknown person.

examples.text: Муж подарил ей великолепный букет цветов.
examples.trans: Her husband gave her a magnificent bouquet of flowers.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'thing', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('things, belongings') (plural 'вещи') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I've brought you your things.
Where are my things?
Everyone has one of these.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.
What delicious tea!

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зможность'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'possibility, opportunity, resource' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('means, resources (plural)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You have some possibilities.
This is a great opportunity.

examples.text: Но ты же ректор! У тебя есть какие-то возможности.
examples.trans: But you're the rector! You have some possibilities.

meanings.note: важный вопрос = an important matter
важный вопрос = an important matter

examples.trans: I have a question.
It's a very important matter.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'second', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: This is my second term.
The second lesson is hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fried eggs, sunny-side-up eggs' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: For breakfast we prepared sunny-side-up eggs.

examples.text: Сегодня мы приготовим простую аппетитную глазунью.
examples.trans: Today we will prepare simple appetizing sunny-side-up eggs.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

examples.trans: I'm ready!
Lunch is ready.
Right, I'm ready!

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'давать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
Some water, please.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: Good afternoon!
I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.en: to add, supplement, put in as an addition
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавлять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to add'.

examples.text: Я добавляю свежую зелень и соус.
examples.trans: I add fresh greens and sauce.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.
Add the dye slowly and carefully.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.trans: Good evening!
She is very kind.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's life.
I want a different life.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'breakfast', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Breakfast hasn't gone cold yet.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на завтрак?
examples.trans: What do we have for breakfast today?
You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'viewer', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Наш зритель больше любит криминальные новости.
examples.trans: Our audience prefers crime news much more.
The viewers want to see a real chef.

examples.text: Все зрители будут свидетелями нашего спора.
examples.trans: All viewers will be witnesses of our bet.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: sometimes, from time to time, occasionally
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'sometimes'.

examples.trans: Sometimes a person makes astonishing discoveries.
Sometimes we do foolish things.

examples.text: Иногда наши победы бывают слишком странными.
examples.trans: Sometimes our victories turn out too strange.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.trans: I'm looking for a job.
What are you looking for?

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'every', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Every day.
Every person.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Secondary conversational sense ('beloved, darling') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!
This is my favourite book.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'butter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Add a piece of butter to the pan.

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

examples.text: Добавляем немного сливочного масла и соли.
examples.trans: We add a little butter and salt.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'moment, instant' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Value every moment of your life.

examples.text: Цените каждый миг своей настоящей жизни.
examples.trans: Value every moment of your real life.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: + genitive plural in nominative/accusative

examples.trans: Several million views already!
I waited a few minutes.

examples.text: Ой, смотрите, Самсона по телевизору показывают! Уже несколько миллионов просмотров!
examples.trans: Oh, look, they're showing Samson on television! Several million views already!

meanings.note: used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.
No! Never!

examples.text: Я никогда в жизни не пробовал такой вкусной утки!
examples.trans: I have never in my life tasted such delicious duck!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.trans: A new house.
I need a new job.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

оказываться.gloss: to turn out to be, prove to be

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be, find oneself
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, prove to be', paired with 'оказаться'.

examples.trans: Simple things turn out to be important.

examples.text: Иногда простые вещи оказываются самыми важными.
examples.trans: Sometimes simple things turn out to be the most important.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'answer', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Thank you for the honest answer.
An exact answer.
Nobody knows the exact answer.

meanings.note: a door, window, bottle, or business

examples.trans: I'm going to open it now.
They open the shop at nine.
I am opening return fire!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in front of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('before (in time)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дача'). Common feminine noun meaning 'broadcast, TV show' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('transfer, handover') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Десять тысяч за каждую новую передачу.
examples.trans: Ten thousand for each new broadcast.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.trans: I made a cake.
Mum cooked a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'pleasant' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('!') (= Enjoy your meal!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!
He's a very nice person.
Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'simple', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('ordinary, common') (простые люди = ordinary people) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's a simple question.
He's an ordinary man.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.en: to heat up, warm up, re-heat
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'огревать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to heat up, warm up', paired with 'разогреть'.

examples.trans: The cook heats up a big frying pan.

examples.text: Берём свежие яйца и разогреваем сковороду.
examples.trans: We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('early').

examples.trans: Good morning to all early viewers.

examples.text: Доброе утро всем ранним зрителям нашего шоу!
examples.trans: Good morning to all early viewers of our show!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'fresh', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Fresh berries on the table.
I bought fresh bread.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.trans: I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'frying pan', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('skillet') (shallow cooking pan) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Рыба почти готова на горячей сковороде.
examples.trans: The fish is almost ready on the hot pan.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ливочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('creamy, cream').

examples.trans: This is creamy, cream.

examples.text: Это нежная курица в сливочном соусе.
examples.trans: It is tender chicken in cream sauce.

examples.text: Добавляем немного сливочного масла и соли.
examples.trans: We add a little butter and salt.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('complicated, difficult').

examples.trans: Look, there's nothing complicated.
That's a very difficult question.
Danila, let's go. Look, there's nothing complicated.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.trans: He's here again.
Rain again.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'salt', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.
Pass the salt, please.

examples.text: Попробуй! Лук, соль, перец — и всё.
examples.trans: Try it! Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'удьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'fate, destiny, fortune' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The people are interested in his fate.
Such is my fate.
And the people are interested in his fate.

meanings.en: to miss, let slip, overlook, fail to seize
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'пускать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to miss, let slip, overlook', paired with 'упустить'.

examples.trans: One must not miss good opportunities.

examples.text: Главное — никогда не упускать свои возможности.
examples.trans: The main thing is never to miss your opportunities.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'morning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Good morning!
What a lovely morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.trans: A good day.
What a lovely morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.en: to value, to appreciate, to esteem
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to value', forming an aspectual pair with 'оценить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Город высоко ценит вас и вашего мужа.
examples.trans: The city values you and your husband highly.
I really appreciate your help.

examples.text: Слушай, Лёля, я очень ценю, что ты приехала.
examples.trans: Listen, Lyolya, I really appreciate that you came.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: О, это, Аркашенька, бывает очень часто.
examples.trans: Oh, that happens very often, Arkashenka.
We often meet in the park.
I used to come see you often.

meanings.note: From French 'chance' (favorable turn of the dice, from Late Latin 'cadentia').

examples.trans: I've got every chance.
This is your chance.

examples.text: А у меня все шансы есть. Жена, двое детей, не сидел, служил в армии.
examples.trans: And I've got every chance. A wife, two kids, no prison record, I served in the army.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'show', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: It turned out to be a great culinary show.
Stop shouting, it turned out a great show!
Now we will arrange a fun show.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'egg' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Берём свежие яйца и разогреваем сковороду.
examples.trans: We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.
